extracted.intended_audience: ProofWiki contributors and volunteer mathematicians/editors (people who want to add or improve proofs on ProofWiki)
extracted.subtask_description: Tasks and standards for contributing to ProofWiki: adding proofs and articles, expanding or fixing existing proofs and stubs, categorizing pages, and participating in community maintenance. The page lists concrete ‘things to do’, wanted proofs, and where to find help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Add proofs! See this page and this page for specific proofs that users want added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The portal explicitly asks contributors to add proofs and points them to pages listing specific proofs that are wanted. Use the 'wanted proofs' lists as targets for new contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to Top Wanted Proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Top 10 Wanted Proofs (examples listed: Whitney Immersion Theorem; Whitney Embedding Theorem; Topological h-Cobordism Theorem; Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture; Tartaglia's Formula; Burnside's Theorem; Abel–Ruffini Theorem; Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem; Liouville's Theorem (Hamiltonian Mechanics); Liouville's Lemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The portal highlights high-priority theorems that the community would like proofs for — contribute proofs or references for these named items. The list is a concrete target for contributors seeking high-impact additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give explanations or expand parts of proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Give explanations or expand parts of proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve readability and completeness by adding explanatory text and expanding terse or skeletal proof steps. Aim to make proofs understandable without changing their correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand pages that are only stubs
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand pages that are only stubs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify stub articles and flesh them out with formal statements, context, proofs, references, and appropriate links. The portal points to lists of stubs as easy starter tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create articles linked-to but not created
rubrics_metrics.description: Check here for articles linked to but not created, or finish a stub article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow red links (linked-but-missing pages) and create the missing article with a proper statement and proof where applicable. This is an alternative to editing existing pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve issues requiring advanced knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are particularly knowledgeable, you may be able to resolve an issue which the contributors have so far not been able to sort out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tackle difficult or disputed mathematical/technical issues on pages that need expert attention. Such tasks may require subject-matter expertise and careful justification; consult talk pages and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check existing proofs for mistakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit proofs for correctness: identify logical gaps, incorrect steps, unstated assumptions, or misuse of results. Report issues on the talk page or correct them with verifiable reasoning and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to pages containing proofs which may not be valid or complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Contribute to pages containing proofs which may not be valid or complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a proof is incomplete or suspected invalid, supply missing lemmas, clarify arguments, add references, or replace incorrect proofs with corrected ones. Preserve provenance and discuss major changes on the talk page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix up pages that do not look good
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix up pages that do not look good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve formatting, notation consistency, LaTeX rendering, layout, and general presentation. Clean up visually messy pages so proofs and statements are easy to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sure proofs are in the correct categories/subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure proofs are in the correct categories, and subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add or correct category tags so pages appear under appropriate topical indexes. Proper categorization improves discoverability and site organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Help page or ask questions for assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Help with an aspect of ProofWiki: see the help page for documentation, or ask a question for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about formatting, style, or policies, consult the Help page or ask on the site (talk pages or community forums) before making large edits. Follow documented conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss changes on the talk page
rubrics_metrics.description: To discuss this page in more detail, feel free to use the talk page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the page's talk page to coordinate with other contributors, propose substantial edits, and resolve disputes. Keep discussions civil and provide references when arguing correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow community maintenance categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in maintenance tasks listed in the navigation (Proofread Articles, Wanted Proofs, Help Needed, Research Required, Stub Articles, Tidy Articles, Improvements Invited, Refactoring, Missing Links, Maintenance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The portal points to many specialized maintenance queues — pick tasks from these categories according to interest and skill. Each queue implies different expectations (e.g., proofreading vs. research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove WIP template when complete
rubrics_metrics.description: When this work has been completed, you may remove this instance of {{WIP}} from the code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a procedural housekeeping step, remove the 'WIP' template after finishing the indicated work to signal completion. Follow site editing conventions for template removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote the wiki / tell your friends
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase community participation and readership by sharing ProofWiki with peers and on relevant forums; outreach helps recruit contributors who can add proofs and improvements.
